stem:
Meena swings two simple pendulums in her school laboratory in Jaipur. Pendulum P and pendulum Q have the same length, but the bob of pendulum Q is heavier. Both are set swinging with small oscillations at the same place.
Which row correctly describes the time periods of the two pendulums?

options.text: P and Q have the same time period; time period depends on length, not on the mass of the bob
Q has a longer time period; time period increases with the mass of the bob
Q has a shorter time period; time period decreases with the mass of the bob
The time periods cannot be compared unless the place is changed

tables: {"headers":["comparison of time periods","reason"],"rows":[["P and Q equal","time period depends on length, not on bob mass"],["Q longer than P","time period increases with bob mass"],["Q shorter than P","time period decreases with bob mass"],["cannot be compared","place must be changed first"]],"row_labels":["A","B","C","D"],"caption":"","is_option_table":true}

teacher.key_rationale: At a given place, the time period of a simple pendulum depends only on its length (and g), not on the mass of the bob. Since P and Q have the same length at the same place, their time periods are equal, so A is correct. Options B and C trap students who believe a heavier bob swings slower or faster; D traps students who think changing place is needed for comparison.
